violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: Observed PIC touch his face and nose multiple times at the beginning of the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO WASH HANDS AFTER TOUCHING HIS FACE AND BODY PARTS. PIC WASHED HIS HANDS.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours: 1) cooked chopped chicken was observed at 101f. Chicken was cooked 2 hours prior to inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. PIC DISCARDED THE CHICKEN.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: Observed date mark stickers from April and February on multiple containers. Observed no dates on food that was prepared yesterday in the walk-in cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC TO START DATE MARKING CORRECTLY. PEEL OFF OLD DATE MARKING STICKERS AND PUT NEW DATE MARKING STICKERS ON. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH DATE MARKING FACT SHEET.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: 1) chopped chicken was cooled in a COVERED container in the walk-in cooler
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC HOW TO COOL FOODS PROPERLY. COOL FOOD FROM 135f TO 70f IN 2 HOURS OR LESS. IN A TOTAL OF 6 HOURS, COOL FOODS COMPLETELY TO 41f. TRAIN STAFF HOW TO USE THE THERMOMETER TO ENSURE PROPER COOLING. COOL ON SHALLOW PANS AND SPREAD OUT EVENLY. SPEED RACK CAN BE MOVED INTO THE WALK-IN COOLER TO FACILITATE BETTER COOLING. EHS PROVIDED PIC WITH COOLING DOCUMENTS BONCHON RESTON (Inspection Date: 06/27/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) in the 1DR upright hot box, fried chicken drumsticks were observed at 120-130f
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. STAFF REHEATED THE CHICKEN IN THE FRYER TO 168f. REHEATED CHICKEN CAN BE PROPERLY HOT HELD AT 135f OR HOTTER.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) cooked chicken for fried rice was observed at 60f
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. PIC DISCARDED THE CHICKEN

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Observed an unlabeled 1 gallon hand sprayer being stored in the chemical storage area.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. PIC LABELED THE HAND SPRAYER AS DE-GREASER.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Observed boxes of frozen food being stored directly on the floor of the walk-in freezer
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. ELEVATE ALL FOOD TO FACILITATE PROPER CLEANING. BONCHON RESTON (Inspection Date: 01/05/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Plumbing System, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: When turned on, the faucet at the 3-compartment sink was observed leaking and spraying water.
violations.corrective_action: A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair. REPAIR THIS FAUCET.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: corn salad, cooked chicken, kimchi, and sauces in squeeze bottles.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS INSTRUCTED PIC TO LABEL ALL PREPARED FOOD WITH THE DATE IT WAS PREPARED AND THE NAME OF THE FOOD.

violations.title: Food Manager Certificate & Responsibility
violations.observation: There is no Certified Food Manager present at the beginning of the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager. It is highly suggested that you have more than one employee with the food manager's license. ORS Interactive, Inc. (see handout provided) issues the required photo identification card with proof of successful completion of a certified food manager's exam. Failure to have a certified food manager on site during ALL hours of operation including food preparation, food service, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment/utensils will result in closure of the establishment. PIC ARRIVED LATER DURING INSPECTION

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: EHS OBSERVED BREADING STATION FOR FRIED CHICKEN NOT MARKED WITH A 4 HOUR ENDPOINT.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. PIC MARKED BREADING STATION WITH A 4 HOUR ENDPOINT.
